title: Industry Pulse - AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: LEAD - item (w) fired on its first working day: the search layer attributed META'S Agents Rule of Two to SPAIN'S AEPD, and the corrected source is a 326-day-old, archive-ZERO test that The Construct fails on all three legs, including this very job
bullets.summary: A query about the Spanish breach returned a confident paragraph saying the AEPD's February 2026 framework 'established the Rule of 2' and that the breach 'validated the threat model the AEPD identified before the incident occurred.' Both artifacts are real and neither belongs to the other. The AEPD guide exists (18 Feb 2026) and says something else - effective rather than formal human supervision, data minimisation, action logging, DPIA, memory hygiene. The Rule of Two is Meta's, dated 31 October 2025, inspired by Chromium's rule-of-2 and Simon Willison's lethal trifecta. Same failure shape as 06:00, not a second unrelated glitch: FUSION - real parts, real names, false container. Read at the Meta primary: an agent must satisfy no more than two of [A] process untrustworthy inputs, [B] access sensitive systems or private data, [C] change state or communicate externally; if it needs all three without a fresh session it 'should not be permitted to operate autonomously and at a minimum requires supervision.' Archive grep across 84 files: 'Rule of Two' ZERO, 'Rule of 2' ZERO, 'untrustworthy input' ZERO, 'change state' ZERO, 'lethal trifecta' ZERO. Score this job: [A] it reads web results and fetched pages, demonstrably hostile twice in four hours; [B] 06:00 measured 125 skills with ZERO tool restrictions reaching the DreamHost deploy key, GSC, GA4, GitHub and Hermes; [C] launchd com.hartley.pragma-daily commits and pushes its output to the live public dashboard at 06:20 with no human in the loop. All three, every morning, for twenty-one days.
bullets.how: The most serious thing this report has written about itself. (i) The corrected source is a three-line, free, vendor-neutral test that needs no tooling and no budget. (ii) Meta names the cheap fix too - the [AC] one-way switch: run the research leg with no reach into sensitive systems. That is exactly the small follow-on item (c) opened at 06:00 (write disallowed-tools on the credentialed skills), except the Rule of Two tells us WHICH leg to cut and why, which the audit alone did not. (iii) Chasing a false citation is not overhead - the correction is how the real source got read.

bullets.title: The regulatory half, also archive-ZERO: Spain's AEPD has logged the first breach notification in which an AI agent was the instrument that chained the whole attack together
bullets.summary: DECLARED AS AN ARCHIVE MISS, NOT NEWS - dateline 16-17 September, five days old. Archive grep across 84 files: AEPD ZERO, 'data protection authority' ZERO, 'breach notification' ZERO, 'first regulator' ZERO; GDPR in 1 file (20 Aug), 'regulator' in 4, none about this. Read at the primaries: the agent scanned generic files for weaknesses, achieved a successful login, searched the target application on its own until it found a flaw, then used it to modify personal data and reach invoices. Deputy director Francisco Perez Bes is careful - the information comes from the affected organisation's own notification, and using a given model does not mean the model or its provider was compromised. AEPD's framing: 'An agent can receive a goal, plan intermediate tasks, use tools, execute code, consult sources, interpret results, and modify its actions autonomously, based on what it finds.' It demands four changes: adversarial agents enter risk analysis, response times shorten, credentials and digital IDs get real protection, and none of it can be achieved by manual intervention alone.
bullets.how: The other end of bullet 1 - that is the control, this is the filing cabinet it lands in when the control is absent. (i) Together they close the gap item (j) has circled for a week: (j) wanted 'one gate with enforcement power', 20 Sep gave it a conformance contract in OWASP ACS, this fire gives it a free three-line test plus a regulator that has already accepted a filing built on its failure. (ii) PRAGMA read is commercial, not defensive: every client is being sold agent connectors by somebody, AEPD's four demands are a ready-made client checklist, and 'we score your agents against Meta's Rule of Two' costs us nothing to produce. (iii) Item (s) was called 'day three, quiet' at 06:00 and was not quiet - it was unread.

bullets.title: A third agent-drivable browser surface in two fires - ChatGPT's desktop built-in browser takes Chrome extensions, and OpenAI's own docs point users at the Codex Chrome extension precisely when a task needs 'your existing Chrome profile, signed-in session, open tabs'
bullets.summary: DATELINE HANDLED UNDER (w) RATHER THAN ASSERTED: every secondary dates the extension-support addition to 18 September; the vendor primary carries no such date (it reads 'Updated: 15 days ago'), so the FEATURE is confirmed and the DATE is labelled UNCONFIRMED. Archive grep across 84 files: 'in-app browser' ZERO, 'ChatGPT desktop' ZERO, 'extension support' ZERO, '1Password' ZERO; 'Chrome DevTools Protocol', DevTools and CDP each in exactly 1 file (25 Aug). Read at the primary: the built-in browser runs on macOS and Windows with its own browser state and supports richer sign-in, autofill, password management, extensions, downloads and navigation; it asks before using a new website; in a workspace an admin may restrict Browser Use, website access, file transfers, history access or saved approvals.
bullets.how: (i) Item (l) grew a browser at 06:00 and another at 10:00 - in one day, three distinct surfaces: Safari's local MCP server, ChatGPT's built-in browser, and the Codex Chrome extension that explicitly wants the already-open, already-signed-in Chrome. The standing CLAUDE.md rule (never open a new Chrome window, always attach to the already-open Chrome) is now a rule about a surface three vendors are competing to drive. (ii) Read against bullet 1 this is an [A]-amplifier: a browser carrying autofill, password management and a live session is [B] sitting inside the thing that supplies [A]. OpenAI's doc says the quiet part - 'Treat website content as untrusted' - and ships the Rule-of-Two answer without naming it: its own browser state, not your Chrome profile, which is Meta's [AC] configuration. (iii) Item (r): correct partial - not our stack, copy the isolated-profile design.

bullets.title: STANDING ACTIONS - day twenty-one, second fire, as a diff against 06:00; Claude Code lane read at the primary for the EIGHTH consecutive time: still 2.1.278 (19 Sep), no new release in four hours

(b) CHANGED, a third browser surface. (c) closed as an audit, open as a fix, and the fix now has a reason as well as a target. (f) unchanged, 70 days, eighth carried fire. (g) CHANGED TWICE - add ai.meta.com/blog (a lab security blog carrying the control we needed for eleven months, in no lane) and claude.com/blog-category/announcements (fetched today as a vendor primary for the first time; it PROVED the Anthropic lane empty rather than leaving it asserted). (i) DEADLINE IN TWO DAYS (23 Sep). (j) CHANGED, biggest movement on the list - ACS gave it a contract, bullet 1 gives it a test that needs no vendor or budget, bullet 2 gives it a regulator. (k) STILL NOT RUN, 23rd day, now converted from an audit into the [B] MEASUREMENT - the Rule of Two cannot be scored for any other agent without it. (l) CHANGED, eighth day, a second browser in one day. (m) unchanged and worse in context: a remote write path into a corpus that fails all three legs. (o) seventh carried fire. (p) seventh test, SECOND CONSECUTIVE PASS - (c) at 06:00, (j) at 10:00, and neither moved because of a vendor; one moved on a grep, one on an eleven-month-old blog post. (q) FOUR-FOR-FOUR: connectivity, cost, provenance, now configuration. (r) sixth application, correct partial. (s) day three, NOT quiet after all. (t) CHANGED - add a Rule-of-Two configuration column naming which of [A]/[B]/[C] each agent holds; that column is the inventory's whole point and was never there. (u) day two, quiet. (v) day two, PAID OUT AGAIN but the payout was a LAB, not a standards body - (v) is scoped too narrowly. (w) day one, VALIDATED WITHIN FOUR HOURS, different domain, different query, signature named: FUSION. Fifth consecutive lane to validate on day one. NEW (x): THE ARCHIVE FORGETS WHAT IT KILLS - because every fire overwrites the day's file, an item bulleted at 10:00 and killed at 14:00 leaves only its kill LABEL; proof this fire, the 'Irregular four-lab timeline' survives as five words in one KILLED list while 'Heather Adkins', 'capture the flag', 'test environment', 'public repository' and 'undirected' are ZERO across 84 files. Fix is one line: append fires instead of overwriting them. KILLED ON PROVENANCE (twice today): the 'AEPD Rule of 2' attribution, and four undated Anthropic items (Smart reports, geo-pinned inference, budget controls, GitHub-loaded skills - all already in the archive from 11-18 Sep). REPORTED HONESTLY RATHER THAN EMPTY: Anthropic nothing datelined 20-21 Sep, checked for the first time at Anthropic's own announcements index (newest: Projects redesigned, 17 Sep); Claude Code no release since 2.1.278; frontier models nothing on a seventh check; MCP servers nothing new since Safari 27, weekly index unchanged and still headed 'Week of September 20'; funding nothing in window; arXiv nothing datelined 20-21 Sep, 2605.18991 surfaced under (v) but its dateline was not read at the page, so NAMED NOT BULLETED under (w).
bullets.how: One lane validated on day one ((w)), one lane re-scoped ((v)), one item moved substantively ((j)), one new item ((x)), and the list passed its own test for the second consecutive fire.

praxis_lesson: THE CONTROL WE HAVE BEEN INVENTING FOR TWENTY-ONE DAYS WAS PUBLISHED ON 31 OCTOBER 2025, IS THREE LINES LONG, IS FREE, AND THIS REPORT FAILS IT EVERY MORNING AT 06:20 WHEN IT PUSHES ITSELF TO A PUBLIC WEBSITE WITH NO HUMAN IN THE LOOP. Meta's Agents Rule of Two: an agent may hold at most two of [A] untrusted input, [B] access to sensitive systems or private data, [C] the ability to change state or communicate externally - and if it needs all three, it should not be permitted to operate autonomously. This job reads the open web ([A]), runs inside a 125-skill corpus with zero tool restrictions reaching the DreamHost deploy key, GSC, GA4, GitHub and Hermes ([B]), and writes files that launchd commits and pushes live ([C]). Three of three, twenty-one days running, and 'Rule of Two' is ZERO across all 84 archive files. Yesterday's lesson said the source list is made entirely of parties with something to sell, and item (v) answered 'grep the standards bodies.' Today's correction is narrower and more embarrassing: this one was not at a standards body either - it was on a frontier lab's security blog, a lane we read every day for model launches and never once for method. SECOND, AND IT IS THE REASON WE FOUND IT AT ALL: ITEM (w), WRITTEN FOUR HOURS AGO, FIRED AGAIN - AND THE SECOND FIRING NAMES THE MECHANISM. At 06:00 the search layer fused four real Claude Code releases into a version number that does not exist. At 10:00 it fused Meta's Rule of Two into the AEPD's February guide, complete with the satisfying narrative that the regulator had predicted its own first case. Real parts, real names, false container. That is not noise, it is a signature, and it appeared three times before noon. The rule that until this morning looked like hygiene has produced, in one day, one avoided fabrication, one corrected attribution - and through the correction, the single most useful artifact this report has ever surfaced. THIRD, THE ONE BOBBY SHOULD ACT ON, AND IT IS SMALLER THAN IT SOUNDS. Do not restrict 125 skills and do not build the incident log this week. Cut ONE LEG OFF ONE AGENT: give the research jobs - this one first - a disallowed-tools line denying every credentialed skill, so Pulse runs [A] + [C] and holds nothing sensitive. That is Meta's own [AC] configuration, it is follow-on item (c) already opened at 06:00, and it takes about as long as the grep that produced 125/0/0/1. Then run item (k), because the Rule of Two cannot be scored for any other agent until we know which skills reach a secret - twenty-three days is long enough. AND FOURTH, THE QUIET STRUCTURAL ONE: THE ARCHIVE FORGETS WHAT IT KILLS. Every fire overwrites the day's file, so an item bulleted at 10:00 and killed at 14:00 survives only as its own kill label. The Gemini/Irregular story - the biggest recurring story on this beat - exists in the archive as five words in a KILLED list while every substantive term from it is ZERO across 84 files. A report whose memory retains the labels and discards the facts will keep rediscovering its own beat, and will keep calling lanes 'quiet' when they are merely unread. Append the fires. That is one line, and it protects twenty-one days of work.
